svg.text: Глава 14 · Протокол межсетевого взаимодействия IP
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0399:c01–p0441:c01 · PDF 399–441 · printed 398–440
1 · IPv4 packet semantics
Connectionless best effort → each packet processed independently
TTL bounds lifetime / loop persistence
Protocol field identifies upper payload: TCP / UDP / ICMP source examples
Header checksum is recomputed as mutable fields change
Fragment metadata shares the IPv4 header with source/destination addressing
2 · Routing-table decision
Destination network/prefix → next-hop router → outgoing interface
Route sources → connected/stack · static/admin · dynamic protocol
Host-specific /32 can override a broader network route
Several prefix matches → choose longest / most specific
0.0.0.0/0 is the least-specific fallback route
3 · Prefix planning and aggregation
Fixed-length subnetting → equal subnets
VLSM → different prefix lengths for different capacity needs
Mask is not carried in an IPv4 packet → routing state must know prefixes
CIDR aggregation → several contiguous networks summarized by one prefix
Address locality enables useful aggregation in provider/core tables
Source contrasts RIPv2/OSPF mask carriage with old RIP
4 · MTU and fragmentation
Smaller next-link MTU can force IPv4 router fragmentation
Identification groups fragments · offset places fragment · MF marks more
DF forbids fragmentation according to explicit source definition
Routers do not reassemble fragments; destination host does
Missing fragment → incomplete set eventually discarded
Source example later contradicts its DF definition; finding recorded separately
5 · ICMP and active diagnostics
ICMP → report conditions; no lost-packet repair
Destination unreachable → type/code refines cause in source examples
traceroute/tracert → increasing TTL + time-exceeded responses
ping → echo request/reply + loss/RTT sample
Traceroute hop RTT is source↔hop round trip, not inter-router link delay
6 · Mobility and QoS extensions
Mobile IPv4 → home address + home/foreign agent + care-of address + tunnel
IntServ / RSVP → per-flow end-to-end reservation
DiffServ → aggregate traffic classes + DSCP marking
PHB examples → EF / AF / LE / best effort
Source says DiffServ is commonly scoped to one administrative domain
Operational reading rule
Path failure → route/LPM → next hop → link/ARP → TTL → MTU/DF → ICMP evidence → active probes → QoS marking/policy.
Do not modify routes or MTU until the failing layer is identified and before-state is captured.
No current platform-specific route/QoS syntax is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 15 starts at p0442:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
